deck.name: NBA
deck.description: Rules, legendary performances and championship history. Historical questions name their season or year.

questions.prompt: How many players from one NBA team are normally on the court at once?
questions.explanation: Each team plays five players at a time, giving ten active players on the court during live play.

questions.prompt: How long is one regulation NBA quarter?
questions.explanation: NBA regulation consists of four 12-minute quarters, for 48 minutes before any overtime.

questions.prompt: How long is a standard NBA overtime period?
questions.explanation: An NBA overtime period lasts five minutes; another overtime follows if the score is tied.

questions.prompt: How many points is a made free throw worth?
questions.explanation: A successful free throw adds one point, regardless of the type of foul that led to it.

questions.prompt: How many points is a made field goal worth when the shooter is on the three-point line?
questions.explanation: Touching the three-point line puts the shooter in the two-point area.

questions.prompt: What is the full NBA shot-clock duration at the start of a new possession?
questions.explanation: The shot clock gives an offense 24 seconds to attempt a field goal that reaches the rim.

questions.prompt: After a missed shot hits the rim and the offense rebounds it, what does the shot clock normally reset to?
questions.explanation: After an offensive rebound of a shot that hit the rim, the NBA shot clock resets to 14 seconds.

questions.prompt: How high is an NBA basket's rim above the floor?
questions.explanation: The rim is 10 feet above the floor, a height used throughout the NBA.

questions.prompt: How many regulation quarters make up an NBA game?
questions.explanation: Four quarters make up regulation play; each is 12 minutes long.

questions.prompt: How many personal fouls normally disqualify an NBA player?
questions.explanation: Special rules apply if a team has no eligible substitutes remaining.

questions.prompt: Which player scored 100 points in an NBA game on March 2, 1962?
questions.explanation: Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1962.

questions.prompt: Which team did Kobe Bryant score 81 points against in January 2006?
questions.explanation: Bryant?s 81-point performance came against Toronto on January 22, 2006, the second-highest single-game total in NBA history.

questions.prompt: Which team finished the 2015-16 regular season with 73 wins?
questions.explanation: Golden State finished 73?9, setting the NBA record for regular-season wins at the time.

questions.prompt: Which franchise won six NBA championships with Michael Jordan in the 1990s?
questions.explanation: Chicago won three straight titles from 1991?93 and three more from 1996?98 with Jordan.

questions.prompt: How many NBA championships did Bill Russell win as a player?
questions.explanation: Russell won 11 championships with Boston, including eight consecutive titles from 1959 through 1966.

questions.prompt: Which team drafted LeBron James first overall in 2003?
questions.explanation: Cleveland held the first pick in 2003 and selected James, who had grown up in nearby Akron.

questions.prompt: Who coached the Dallas Mavericks to their 2011 NBA championship?
questions.explanation: Rick Carlisle coached Dallas to the 2011 title, the franchise’s first NBA championship.

questions.prompt: How many games did Dallas need to win the 2011 NBA Finals?
questions.explanation: Dallas beat Miami four games to two, clinching the best-of-seven series in six games.

questions.prompt: Which franchise won its first NBA championship in 2019?
questions.explanation: Toronto defeated Golden State in the 2019 Finals to win the franchise?s first championship.

questions.prompt: Which player is famous for the skyhook shot?
questions.explanation: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar?s skyhook was a high-arcing one-handed shot that was difficult for defenders to block.

questions.prompt: Which team did Allen Iverson lead to the 2001 NBA Finals?
questions.explanation: Iverson led Philadelphia past Milwaukee in the Eastern Conference Finals before the 76ers faced the Lakers.

questions.prompt: Which NBA star was nicknamed The Dream?
questions.explanation: Olajuwon?s Houston teammates and fans knew him as The Dream; his footwork in the post helped build that reputation.

questions.prompt: Which franchise did Tim Duncan play for throughout his NBA career?
questions.explanation: Duncan played all 19 NBA seasons for San Antonio, winning five championships with the Spurs.

questions.prompt: Which two jersey numbers did Kobe Bryant wear during his Lakers career?
questions.explanation: Bryant wore No. 8 early in his Lakers career and later switched to No. 24.

questions.prompt: What is the NBA championship trophy called?
questions.explanation: The Finals MVP award is named for Bill Russell.

questions.prompt: In which season did the NBA first use the three-point line?
questions.explanation: The NBA introduced the three-point line in the 1979?80 season.

questions.prompt: A player standing on the three-point line can score three points with that shot.
questions.explanation: A field goal from on the line is worth two points.

questions.prompt: A tied score at the end of NBA regulation play leads to overtime.
questions.explanation: Overtime periods continue until a winner is determined.

questions.prompt: What does a triple-double mean?
questions.answer: Recording at least 10 in three statistical categories in one game, commonly points, rebounds and assists.
questions.explanation: A triple-double means reaching at least 10 in three statistical categories in one game; points, rebounds, and assists are common categories.

questions.prompt: What does MVP stand for?
questions.explanation: MVP is the abbreviation for Most Valuable Player, an award recognizing a season?s or event?s standout player.

questions.prompt: After a team gains control in its backcourt, how long does it have to advance the ball into the frontcourt?
questions.explanation: NBA teams have eight seconds to bring the ball across the division line.

questions.prompt: What happens when an offensive player remains in the lane for more than three seconds while the team controls the ball in the frontcourt?
choices: The offense gets a free throw
The other team receives the ball
The shot clock resets to 14 seconds
questions.explanation: The offensive three-second violation results in loss of possession.

questions.prompt: Under the NBA defensive three-second rule, a defender in the lane must generally do what?
choices: Leave the lane after every made basket
Touch the ball before the shot clock resets
Actively guard an opponent within three seconds
Stand outside the three-point line on defense
questions.explanation: A defender may remain in the lane beyond three seconds only while actively guarding an opponent or during a rule exception.

questions.prompt: How many seconds does an inbounding player generally have to release the ball?
questions.explanation: The thrower-in must release the ball within five seconds after the official places it at the player’s disposal.

questions.prompt: What does a held ball normally lead to under NBA rules?
choices: A jump ball between the players involved
A free throw for the defense
questions.explanation: When opponents have simultaneous control, the referee calls a held ball and awards possession by a jump ball.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a charge and a blocking foul?
choices: A charge is called on a missed shot; blocking is called on a made shot
A charge is illegal offensive contact; blocking is illegal defensive contact
A charge is always a technical foul; blocking is always a flagrant foul
A charge happens outside the paint; blocking happens only inside it
questions.explanation: A charge is a player-control foul by the offense; a blocking foul is illegal contact by a defender.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the restricted-area arc beneath the basket?
choices: It marks the area where offensive players may stay only three seconds
It shows where a player must stand to begin free throws
It limits when a defender can draw a charge directly under the rim
It defines the space where the coach may stand during play
questions.explanation: The restricted area affects block/charge judgments for airborne offensive players near the basket.

questions.prompt: Which violation occurs when a player illegally moves their feet while holding the ball?
questions.explanation: Traveling is illegal foot movement by a player who is holding the ball.

questions.prompt: Which violation is called when the offense returns the ball to its backcourt after establishing frontcourt control, subject to exceptions?
questions.explanation: After frontcourt control is established, the offense generally cannot cause the ball to return to the backcourt and touch it first.

questions.prompt: What is the usual NBA penalty for a defensive three-second violation?
choices: Two free throws and a change of possession to the defense
A technical free throw and continued offensive possession
A jump ball at the center circle between two players
A personal foul on the defender and no free throws
questions.explanation: The NBA assesses a technical foul; the offense retains possession.

questions.prompt: If a three-point shot goes in while the shooter is fouled, what can the shooter earn?
questions.explanation: A made three-pointer counts, and a shooting foul can add one free throw: the four-point play.

questions.prompt: What is the normal result of a legal blocked shot that does not go through the basket?
questions.explanation: A legal block is a live-ball play; either team may recover the ball.

questions.prompt: What was the NBA called before it adopted its current name in 1949?
questions.explanation: The BAA merged with the National Basketball League and became the NBA in 1949.

questions.prompt: Which team won eight consecutive NBA championships from 1959 through 1966?
questions.explanation: Boston’s run from 1959 to 1966 remains the longest consecutive championship streak in NBA history.

questions.prompt: Which franchise selected Magic Johnson first overall in the 1979 NBA Draft?
questions.explanation: The Lakers selected Magic Johnson with the first pick of the 1979 draft.

questions.prompt: Which team did Michael Jordan and the Chicago Bulls defeat for their first NBA title in 1991?
questions.explanation: Chicago beat the Lakers in five games in the 1991 Finals.

questions.prompt: Which former ABA feature did the NBA adopt before the 1979–80 season?
questions.explanation: The three-point line originated in the ABA and was adopted by the NBA in 1979–80.

questions.prompt: Who became the first Black player to appear in an NBA game, in 1950?
questions.explanation: Earl Lloyd debuted for the Washington Capitols on October 31, 1950. Chuck Cooper and Nat Clifton also broke the barrier in 1950, but Lloyd played first.

questions.prompt: Which team did the Cleveland Cavaliers defeat to win their first NBA championship in 2016?
questions.explanation: Cleveland beat Golden State in seven games, completing the first 3–1 Finals comeback.

questions.prompt: Which team did Denver defeat in the 2023 NBA Finals?
questions.explanation: Denver defeated Miami in five games to win the 2023 NBA Finals.

questions.prompt: Who won the 2025 NBA Finals MVP award after Oklahoma City’s championship?
questions.explanation: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander won Finals MVP after Oklahoma City defeated Indiana in the 2025 Finals.

questions.prompt: Which franchise won the 2025–26 NBA championship?
questions.explanation: The Knicks defeated the Spurs in the 2026 Finals, winning their first title since 1973.

questions.prompt: Which team did the Los Angeles Lakers defeat in the 2020 NBA Finals?
questions.explanation: The Lakers defeated Miami in six games in the 2020 Finals.

questions.prompt: Which team did the Golden State Warriors beat to win the 2022 NBA Finals?
questions.explanation: Golden State defeated Boston in six games for its fourth title of the Stephen Curry era.

questions.prompt: Which team won the 2015 NBA Finals against Cleveland?
questions.explanation: Golden State defeated Cleveland in six games for its first title since 1975.

questions.prompt: Which franchise did the Detroit Pistons defeat in the 2004 Finals?
questions.explanation: Detroit defeated the Lakers in five games in the 2004 Finals.

questions.prompt: Which team did the Dallas Mavericks defeat to win the 2011 NBA Finals?
questions.explanation: Dallas defeated Miami in six games for the franchise’s first NBA championship.

questions.prompt: Which NBA champion did San Antonio defeat in the 2014 Finals?
questions.explanation: San Antonio defeated the two-time defending champion Miami Heat in five games.

questions.prompt: Who was named the 2019 NBA Finals MVP after Toronto won its first championship?
questions.explanation: Kawhi Leonard won Finals MVP after leading Toronto to a six-game victory over Golden State.

questions.prompt: Who was named Finals MVP when Denver won its first title in 2023?
questions.explanation: Nikola Jokic received the Bill Russell Finals MVP award after Denver’s 2023 title run.

questions.prompt: Who was the 2024 NBA Finals MVP?
questions.explanation: Jaylen Brown won Finals MVP after Boston’s 2024 championship.

questions.prompt: Which player became the first unanimous NBA regular-season MVP in 2016?
questions.explanation: Curry received all 131 first-place votes for the 2015–16 MVP award.

questions.prompt: Which player won three consecutive NBA regular-season MVP awards from 1984 through 1986?
questions.explanation: Larry Bird won MVP in each of the 1983–84, 1984–85, and 1985–86 seasons.

questions.prompt: Which player won the 2014 NBA Finals MVP award?
questions.explanation: Kawhi Leonard received Finals MVP honors as San Antonio defeated Miami.

questions.prompt: What is the NBA Finals MVP award named for?
questions.explanation: The Bill Russell NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award honors the Celtics center who won 11 championships.

questions.prompt: Which player won the NBA’s first Defensive Player of the Year award, in 1983–84?
questions.explanation: Sidney Moncrief of Milwaukee was the first recipient of the award.

questions.prompt: Which statistic is calculated as made field goals divided by attempted field goals?
questions.explanation: Field-goal percentage measures how often field-goal attempts are made.

questions.prompt: Which statistic records a pass that directly leads to a teammate’s made basket?
questions.explanation: An assist is credited for a pass that leads directly to a made field goal.

questions.prompt: What does a player’s plus-minus measure while that player is on court?
choices: The player’s shooting accuracy during those minutes
The player’s rebound total during those minutes
The team’s scoring margin during those minutes
The number of fouls the player drew in those minutes
questions.explanation: Plus-minus is the difference between the team’s points scored and allowed while a player is on the floor.

questions.prompt: Who holds the NBA regular-season record for most career assists?
questions.explanation: Stockton finished his career with 15,806 regular-season assists, the NBA record.

questions.prompt: Which player became the NBA’s all-time regular-season scoring leader in 2023?
questions.explanation: LeBron James passed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar’s regular-season scoring total in February 2023.

questions.prompt: Which player holds the NBA career record for made three-point field goals?
questions.explanation: Stephen Curry passed Ray Allen’s previous career record and has extended the mark.

questions.prompt: What does a rebound record?
choices: A pass that leads directly to a teammate’s made basket
A made shot attempted from behind the three-point arc
Recovery of the ball after a missed field-goal or free-throw attempt
A change of possession awarded after a defensive foul
questions.explanation: A rebound is credited to a player who secures the ball after a missed shot.

questions.prompt: Which team won the inaugural BAA championship in 1947?
questions.explanation: The Philadelphia Warriors won the first Basketball Association of America championship in 1947; the BAA later became the NBA.

questions.prompt: Which franchise drafted Kobe Bryant in 1996 before trading him to the Lakers?
questions.explanation: Charlotte selected Bryant with the 13th pick and traded his rights to the Lakers on draft night.

questions.prompt: Which team selected Dirk Nowitzki in the 1998 draft before trading him to Dallas?
questions.explanation: Milwaukee drafted Nowitzki ninth overall and immediately traded him to Dallas.

questions.prompt: Which player was selected first overall in the 2004 draft by Orlando?
questions.explanation: The Orlando Magic selected Dwight Howard first overall in 2004.

questions.prompt: Which player did Cleveland select first overall in 2011?
questions.explanation: Cleveland chose Kyrie Irving with the first pick of the 2011 draft.

questions.prompt: Which team selected Victor Wembanyama first overall in 2023?
questions.explanation: San Antonio selected Wembanyama with the first pick of the 2023 NBA Draft.

questions.prompt: Which franchise did Tim Duncan help lead to five NBA championships?
questions.explanation: Duncan spent his entire NBA career with San Antonio and won five titles.

questions.prompt: Which service academy did David Robinson attend before his NBA career?
questions.explanation: Robinson played college basketball at the U.S. Naval Academy and served in the Navy before joining the NBA.

questions.prompt: Which player was called “The Round Mound of Rebound”?
questions.explanation: Barkley was known for rebounding despite being shorter than many power forwards.

questions.prompt: Which NBA great was nicknamed “The Logo”?
questions.explanation: West’s silhouette inspired the NBA logo, leading to the nickname.

questions.prompt: Which franchise plays its home games at Madison Square Garden?
questions.explanation: Madison Square Garden in Manhattan is the Knicks’ home arena.

questions.prompt: Which team plays its home games at the United Center?
questions.explanation: The Bulls share Chicago’s United Center with the NHL’s Blackhawks.

questions.prompt: Which NBA franchise is based in Salt Lake City?
questions.explanation: The Utah Jazz play in Salt Lake City; the franchise began in New Orleans.

questions.prompt: Which franchise moved from Seattle to Oklahoma City in 2008?
questions.explanation: The Seattle SuperSonics relocated and became the Oklahoma City Thunder.

questions.prompt: Which team is based in the San Francisco Bay Area?
questions.explanation: The Warriors play at Chase Center in San Francisco.

questions.prompt: Which number of games must a team win to take a best-of-seven NBA playoff series?
questions.explanation: Four wins are enough to clinch a best-of-seven series.

questions.prompt: How many rounds does a team normally win to become NBA champion?
questions.explanation: The postseason has four rounds: first round, conference semifinals, conference finals, and NBA Finals.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the NBA Play-In Tournament?
choices: To determine the final playoff seeds in each conference
To decide the regular-season MVP before the playoffs
To set the draft lottery order for non-playoff teams
To decide the NBA champion in a single-game final
questions.explanation: The tournament determines the seventh and eighth seeds from teams near the playoff cutoff.

questions.prompt: The NBA Finals match the champions of which two groups?
questions.explanation: The Eastern Conference champion plays the Western Conference champion in the NBA Finals.

questions.prompt: The NBA uses an alternating-possession arrow after every held ball.
questions.explanation: The NBA generally resolves held balls with a jump ball rather than an alternating-possession arrow.

questions.prompt: What does “and-one” mean in basketball?
questions.answer: A player makes a field goal while being fouled and receives one additional free throw.
questions.explanation: The phrase describes a made basket plus the opportunity for one free throw after a shooting foul.

questions.prompt: What is a pick-and-roll?
questions.answer: An offensive action in which a player sets a screen for the ball handler and then moves toward the basket or open space.
questions.explanation: The screen can free the ball handler while the screener rolls toward the rim or a passing lane.

questions.prompt: What is a fast break?
questions.answer: A quick offensive attack immediately after gaining possession, before the defense is set.
questions.explanation: Teams try to create a scoring chance before defenders can organize.

questions.prompt: What is a double-double?
questions.answer: A game in which a player reaches at least 10 in two statistical categories.
questions.explanation: Common combinations include points and rebounds or points and assists.

questions.prompt: What does “box out” mean?
questions.answer: To use body position to keep an opponent away from the basket while pursuing a rebound.
questions.explanation: Boxing out helps a player gain rebounding position after a missed shot.

questions.prompt: What is a “sweep” in a playoff series?
questions.answer: Winning every game in the series without a loss.
questions.explanation: A four-game sweep is the quickest possible outcome in a best-of-seven series.

questions.prompt: What is home-court advantage in an NBA playoff series?
questions.answer: The higher-seeded team hosts more games in the series.
questions.explanation: In a best-of-seven series, the higher seed hosts Games 1, 2, 5, and 7.

questions.prompt: What does “rim protection” describe?
questions.answer: Defensive play near the basket that deters or contests shots at the rim.
questions.explanation: Rim protectors use positioning and shot contests to make close attempts harder.
